about: How different the pod's rings are from one another, against the film's logograms among themselves (Luis, 2026-11-18: 'ours look very similar, why is that? did we add enough variance?'). Measure: the gate's coarse marks similarity (research/ip_probe/simprobe.py: 360 x 96 polar, the base ring band removed, rotation and mirror invariant). Rings: the 126 of the three gate species at 1100 px; identical rasters (two scenes the species writes with the same words) counted once. Outcomes of F4-P7 and F4-P8 (predictions.json). Numbers only.

singleMassNearestOther.note: like for like with the pod, whose rings are one clause each

singleMassAllPairs.note: like for like for rings that share no word; 'full' keeps the base ring, which the eye sees and the gate's marks layer removes

inkfig-0.5.reading: the look did not follow the meaning: rings sharing no word were as alike as rings one word apart

inkfig-0.6.reading: the look follows the meaning (the more words two rings share, the more alike), but every ring of the pod has one grammar, so one skeleton, and the larger masses raised the level
inkfig-0.6.readingFull: with the ring kept, the meaning gradient vanishes: the same heavy, even ring in every figure outweighs what the words do
